mechanics.behavior: Straight-line nine-instruction body. The receiver is aliased into ESI; the address of the incoming property-id word is pushed as the port's only stack argument; ECX is set to the receiver word at displacement 0x18 and 0x006a2cb0 is called; the receiver word at displacement 0x34 is then incremented unconditionally; ESI is restored and the property-id word is popped by RET 0x4.

callee_shape.argument_is_consumed_by_callee: yes: both of the port's exits are RET 0x4 (0x006a2d16, 0x006a2d1e), so it pops the pointer itself; 0x006a2ef0 pushes and does not pop
callee_shape.result: EAX, returned to this function's caller unchanged

unresolved_questions: The 0x34 receiver word is incremented on every call, including when the port reports no removal, but nothing in the machine record establishes what it counts. The port's own listing places its 0x18-stride entry region immediately below that word (see mechanics.callee_receiver_observations), which makes a version or mutation counter a plausible reading; the sibling body at 0x006a2a80 increments the same displacement after its own mutation. Both are hypotheses, not evidence for this function.

The sub-object at receiver + 0x18 is the receiver 0x006a2cb0 operates on, but the machine-derived receiver record does not enumerate that displacement (the LEA is not a memory access) and no type record establishes what that sub-object is; only 0x006a2cb0's own decompilation shows it behaving as a contiguous array of 0x18-byte entries.

The return width class is unresolved: the ABI envelope records register_class aggregate_unknown and return.type null, so 'int' rests on the resolved Ghidra prototype plus the pass-through of EAX, not on a width classification.
Whether callers of RemoveProperty depend on the 0/1 range the port returns, and whether the increment is expected to happen even when the port reports no removal, are not established by this body.

No direct caller xref exists; the two table references at 0x01408838 and 0x01408888 are the only reachability evidence and no original-process trace was captured, so the calling convention and argument order have not been exercised at runtime.

conditions: A caller reaches 0x006a2ef0 through one of the two table references and supplies a live property list.
The removal port 0x006a2cb0 returns both of its observed results (an entry removed and no entry removed) on the same caller path.
A runtime trace records the value of the receiver word at displacement 0x34 before and after the call, and confirms the property-id word is passed by address.
